expectations.text: The check command exits 0 (suite passes; dueDate is correct in seven time zones from UTC-11 to UTC+14 across month, year, leap-day and DST boundaries; a new test fails against the original lib/ code even on a machine running in UTC)
Before fixing, the agent reproduced the symptom by running the code or tests under a US Pacific time zone (TZ or process.env.TZ) and shows the failing result
expectations.evidence: The final message says that while explaining the original bug, the agent "ran them with the timezone set to `America/Los_Angeles` and 3 of the 4 failed", so it reproduced and reported the failure under Pacific time. Only the final message is available as evidence, not the run transcript.

expectations.text: The final message names the root cause: the date-only string is parsed as UTC midnight while setDate/getDate and the formatting use local time, so zones behind UTC land on the previous day
expectations.evidence: The message says "`new Date('2026-03-01')` reads a date-only string as midnight UTC. The code then worked with it in the server's local time. In California, midnight UTC is 4–5 pm the day before, so every due date came out one day early."

expectations.text: The fix uses one consistent frame for parsing, arithmetic and formatting (all UTC or all local) rather than adding a day conditionally or special-casing particular zones
expectations.evidence: The diff parses with `Date.UTC(y, mo - 1, d)`, adds days with `setUTCDate(d.getUTCDate() + days)` and formats with `getUTCFullYear/getUTCMonth/getUTCDate`, so every step is UTC and nothing is special-cased for particular zones.
